# httpbin

httpbin.org - echoes HTTP requests back; every request shape, as a reference

- **Base URL:** https://httpbin.org
- **Described in:** config/api.yaml
- **APIs:** 12, with 12 examples verified against the service

## How to use it

Each API below has an example curl command. It runs in a shell, or from Claude's Bash tool, once each value in angle brackets, such as `<id>`, is filled in.

- **Shell:** `curldex httpbin` lists the APIs; `curldex httpbin <api>` shows one, with its example.
- **IPython:** build a command, and run it with `!`:

  ```python
  import curldex
  app = curldex.load_app("httpbin")
  app.apis()
  cmd = app.curl("get-query")
  !{cmd} | jq .
  ```

- **Access levels:** *read* APIs only read data; *write* APIs create or change it; *destructive* APIs delete or replace it, so run those only when that's intended, after checking the target.
- **Debugging:** add `-D -` to see the response headers, or `-o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'` for just the status (in IPython, double the braces).

## Authentication

**Type:** `none`. The service needs no credentials; the commands have no `-K`.

## APIs

| API             | Access      | Method | Path             | Description                                                                |
|-----------------|-------------|--------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| get-query       | read        | GET    | /get             | Query params of each type; answers with what it received in args           |
| get-headers     | read        | GET    | /headers         | A header param; answers with the request's headers                         |
| get-path        | read        | GET    | /anything/{path} | A path value that keeps its slashes (reserved)                             |
| get-status      | read        | GET    | /status/{code}   | Answers with the given HTTP status and no body                             |
| post-json       | write       | POST   | /post            | A JSON body built from fields; answers with it in json                     |
| post-whole-json | write       | POST   | /post            | A whole JSON body given as one value (in json)                             |
| post-form       | write       | POST   | /post            | A form body (application/x-www-form-urlencoded); nested values in brackets |
| upload-file     | write       | POST   | /post            | A multipart body with a text field and a file                              |
| post-raw        | write       | POST   | /post            | A raw body sent as it is, with its own Content-Type                        |
| put-json        | write       | PUT    | /put             | A PUT; httpbin stores nothing, so it replaces nothing                      |
| patch-json      | write       | PATCH  | /patch           | A PATCH                                                                    |
| delete-anything | destructive | DELETE | /delete          | A DELETE (destructive by its method, though httpbin deletes nothing)       |

### get-query

`GET /get`: **read** (reads data)

Query params of each type; answers with what it received in args

| Param | In    | Type    | Required / default | Description               |
|-------|-------|---------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| q     | query | string  |                    | Text                      |
| limit | query | integer | default 10         |                           |
| exact | query | boolean |                    |                           |
| tags  | query | array   |                    | Repeated as tags=a&tags=b |
| sort  | query | string  |                    | One of: new, old.         |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' 'https://httpbin.org/get?q=curldex&limit=3&exact=true&tags=a&tags=b&sort=new'
```

Response: `{args: {exact: string, limit: string, q: string, sort: string, tags[]: string}, headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}, origin: string, url: string}`

### get-headers

`GET /headers`: **read** (reads data)

A header param; answers with the request's headers

| Param  | In     | Type   | Required / default | Description                                                               |
|--------|--------|--------|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| X-Demo | header | string |                    | Any text (httpbin's load balancer drops some names, such as X-Request-Id) |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' -H 'X-Demo: hello' 'https://httpbin.org/headers'
```

Response: `{headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}}`

### get-path

`GET /anything/{path}`: **read** (reads data)

A path value that keeps its slashes (reserved)

| Param | In   | Type   | Required / default | Description             |
|-------|------|--------|--------------------|-------------------------|
| path  | path | string | required           | Any path, such as a/b/c |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' 'https://httpbin.org/anything/a/b/c'
```

Response: `{args: {}, data: string, files: {}, form: {}, headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}, json: null, method: string, origin: string, url: string}`

### get-status

`GET /status/{code}`: **read** (reads data)

Answers with the given HTTP status and no body

| Param | In   | Type    | Required / default | Description                 |
|-------|------|---------|--------------------|-----------------------------|
| code  | path | integer | required           | An HTTP status, such as 204 |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 204):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' 'https://httpbin.org/status/204'
```

### post-json

`POST /post`: **write** (creates or changes data)

A JSON body built from fields; answers with it in json

| Param | In   | Type    | Required / default | Description     |
|-------|------|---------|--------------------|-----------------|
| title | body | string  | required           |                 |
| count | body | integer |                    |                 |
| meta  | body | object  |                    | Any JSON object |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' --json '{"title": "Hello", "count": 2, "meta": {"team": "core"}}' 'https://httpbin.org/post'
```

Response: `{args: {}, data: string, files: {}, form: {}, headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}, json: {count: integer, meta: {team: string}, title: string}, origin: string, url: string}`

### post-whole-json

`POST /post`: **write** (creates or changes data)

A whole JSON body given as one value (in json)

| Param | In   | Type   | Required / default | Description |
|-------|------|--------|--------------------|-------------|
| body  | json | object | required           |             |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' --json '{"title": "Hello", "items": [1, 2]}' 'https://httpbin.org/post'
```

Response: `{args: {}, data: string, files: {}, form: {}, headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}, json: {items[]: integer, title: string}, origin: string, url: string}`

### post-form

`POST /post`: **write** (creates or changes data); form body

A form body (application/x-www-form-urlencoded); nested values in brackets

| Param | In   | Type   | Required / default | Description                 |
|-------|------|--------|--------------------|-----------------------------|
| name  | body | string | required           |                             |
| meta  | body | object |                    | Sent as meta[key]=value     |
| tags  | body | array  |                    | Sent as tags[0]=a&tags[1]=b |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' --data-urlencode 'name=Ada Lovelace' --data-urlencode 'meta[team]=core' --data-urlencode 'tags[0]=x' --data-urlencode 'tags[1]=y' 'https://httpbin.org/post'
```

Response: `{args: {}, data: string, files: {}, form: {<key>: string, name: string}, headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}, json: null, origin: string, url: string}`

### upload-file

`POST /post`: **write** (creates or changes data); multipart body (files as @path)

A multipart body with a text field and a file

| Param   | In   | Type   | Required / default | Description         |
|---------|------|--------|--------------------|---------------------|
| caption | body | string |                    |                     |
| file    | body | file   | required           | A local file's path |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' --form-string 'caption=a test file' -F 'file=@"<path_to_a_file>"' 'https://httpbin.org/post'
```

Response: `{args: {}, data: string, files: {file: string}, form: {caption: string}, headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}, json: null, origin: string, url: string}`

### post-raw

`POST /post`: **write** (creates or changes data); raw body (text/plain)

A raw body sent as it is, with its own Content-Type

| Param | In   | Type   | Required / default | Description |
|-------|------|--------|--------------------|-------------|
| text  | json | string | required           |             |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -H 'Accept: application/json' -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data-raw 'line one
line two' 'https://httpbin.org/post'
```

Response: `{args: {}, data: string, files: {}, form: {}, headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}, json: null, origin: string, url: string}`

### put-json

`PUT /put`: **write** (creates or changes data)

A PUT; httpbin stores nothing, so it replaces nothing

| Param | In   | Type   | Required / default | Description |
|-------|------|--------|--------------------|-------------|
| title | body | string |                    |             |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -X PUT -H 'Accept: application/json' --json '{"title": "Hello"}' 'https://httpbin.org/put'
```

Response: `{args: {}, data: string, files: {}, form: {}, headers: {Accept: string, <key>: string, Host: string}, json: {title: string}, origin: string, url: string}`

`PATCH /patch`: **write** (creates or changes data)

A PATCH

| Param | In   | Type   | Required / default | Description |
|-------|------|--------|--------------------|-------------|
| title | body | string |                    |             |

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -X PATCH -H 'Accept: application/json' --json '{"title": "Hello"}' 'https://httpbin.org/patch'
```

### delete-anything

`DELETE /delete`: **destructive** (deletes or replaces data)

A DELETE (destructive by its method, though httpbin deletes nothing)

Example, verified on 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200):

```bash
curl -q -sS -g --compressed -X DELETE -H 'Accept: application/json' 'https://httpbin.org/delete'
```
